unit.title: Indirect object pronouns
unit.subtitle: me, te, le, nos, os, les — saying to/for whom

grammar.title: To whom? For whom? Meet the indirect object
grammar.intro: The indirect object pronoun tells you to whom or for whom something happens. In Le doy el libro a Ana (I give the book to Ana), the book is the direct object and Ana is the indirect one — the person receiving. These little words appear constantly, so let's lock them in.

sections.heading: The six forms
sections.body: Notice they match the direct-object pronouns except for the third person, where both singular and plural use le / les regardless of gender:

sections.heading: Where it goes
sections.body: Placement works just like direct-object pronouns: before the conjugated verb, or attached to an infinitive or gerund.

ex.en: I'm going to explain the plan to him.
I'm going to explain the plan to him.

sections.heading: Doubling with 'a + person'
sections.body: Spanish often uses the pronoun and names the person with a + [person] in the same sentence. It sounds redundant to English ears, but it's completely normal — even required with le / les.

ex.en: I give the book to Ana.

sections.heading: le/les → se before lo/la/los/las
sections.body: When an indirect le or les meets a direct lo/la/los/las, the le/les turns into se. So "I give it to him" is Se lo doy, never "le lo doy".

ex.en: I'll send it to them tomorrow.

takeaways: Indirect object = to/for whom: me, te, le, nos, os, les.
Third person is le (singular) and les (plural), regardless of gender.
Place it before the conjugated verb, or attach it to an infinitive/gerund.
le/les become se before lo/la/los/las: Se lo doy, not 'le lo doy'.
Spanish often doubles: Le doy el libro a Ana.

mistakes.why: le/les turn into se before lo/la/los/las.
The people are plural (mis padres), so use les, not le.

mistakes.w: Yo doy a Ana el libro.
mistakes.r: Le doy el libro a Ana.
mistakes.why: Spanish uses the pronoun le even when the person is named.

exercises.prompt_en: I give the book to Ana.
exercises.no: Ana is one person → “le”: Le doy el libro a Ana.

exercises.prompt_en: The book? I'll give it to him tomorrow.
exercises.no: le/les turn into se before lo → “Se lo doy”.

exercises.prompt_en: The letter? I'll send it to her.
exercises.hint: The letter (la carta) is feminine singular.
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! Se la mando = I send it to her.
exercises.no: La carta is feminine → “se la”: Se la mando.

exercises.prompt: Match each person to its indirect object pronoun.

exercises.no: It was: “Se lo doy a él.” (I give it to him.)
